findings.summary: AC2 and multiple code comments invoke 'retention policy' but no retention policy (TTL/expiry/scheduled deletion) is actually implemented anywhere — persistence is indefinite, which trivially satisfies 'retained' but isn't a policy.

'Securely stored' is satisfied only via ownership-scoped access control; there is no separate object storage, encryption-at-rest, or signed-URL mechanism — the raw image string (URL or base64) is written verbatim into a Postgres text column. Disclosed/intentional scope cut (AC1 out of scope), not a fabrication, but the word 'securely' outruns what's implemented.

note: Self-evaluator condition: full repo/spec/builder-context access is expected and allowed per the context boundary table, so isolation-manifest enforcement is a lighter-weight sanity check here than for the independent condition (this run was not launched with a formal violation-detection wrapper; resourceUse/actionsArtifact/isolationManifestArtifact digests above are placeholders pending a follow-up instrumentation pass, not fabricated measurements — flagged honestly rather than invented).
